# Legendary Retreats — Be Legendary

> Be Legendary designs and leads immersive, fully custom executive leadership retreats for CEOs and their senior leadership teams. Every retreat is engineered around one outcome the client defines, then reinforced for 30 days afterward so the behavioral change is measurable — not momentary. Founded and led by James Carter, with 25 years inside executive teams.

## What makes Legendary Retreats different
- **Function before format.** We begin with two questions — "What do you want your people walking away feeling, thinking, and saying to one another?" and "If you could achieve only one thing on this retreat, what would it be?" The answer defines the *function*; every element of the retreat is then engineered to serve it.
- **Format follows function.** The environment, activities, and conversations are chosen for the outcome, never for how they photograph. Formats are interchangeable tools: off-road immersion, open-water sailing, jungle trek, remote lodge ("cabin fever"), five-star estate, horseback/ranch, high-alpine expedition — and, when it serves the outcome, deliberately rough settings like an 1800s mining lodge.
- **30-day reinforcement.** Daily behavioral prompts, tracking, and facilitator re-engagement after the retreat, closing with a behavioral-change report measured against a baseline. One $3B enterprise leadership team posted a 209% mindset-score gain measured 30 days post-retreat.
- **Led by James Carter.** 25 years inside executive teams; hundreds of executive leadership-team retreats designed and led. Co-author alongside Stephen Covey, Ken Blanchard, Deepak Chopra, and Brian Tracy. Featured by CNN, CNN Money, and Business Insider.
- **Social enterprise.** Every executive who attends funds a leadership workshop for a young person aged 12–15.

## Who it's for
CEOs and senior leadership teams of roughly 5–12, most often at companies scaling through real complexity where executive misalignment carries a measurable cost.

## Where
Most retreats run across the United States (40 of 50 states to date), with select retreats in Central America and worldwide on request. Example U.S. destinations: Moab UT, the San Juan Mountains CO, the Sierra Nevada and Great Basin Desert, Sedona AZ, Montana & the Rockies, Death Valley CA.

## Investment
Most multi-day executive retreats for a team of 8–12 run $75,000–$500,000, fully turnkey (facilitation, lodging, meals, activities, transfers, and the 30-day reinforcement system).

- [Leadership Retreats](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/leadership-retreats): The full method — function-first design, format-follows-function, the A→B→reinforcement system, outcomes, and investment.
- [Destinations](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/destinations): U.S.-first destination guide with detail pages for the San Juan Mountains (CO), Moab (UT), the Sierra Nevada (CA), the Great Basin Desert (NV), and Death Valley (CA).
- [Field Notes](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/field-notes): Essays by James Carter. Key pieces: "Do leadership retreats actually work?"; "The two questions that define a great leadership retreat" (function before format); "How to align a leadership team pulling in different directions"; "12 questions to ask before any executive retreat" (planning checklist); "What a 30-day reinforcement actually looks like"; "What is an experiential leadership retreat?" (format follows function, retreats are workouts, growth happens in recovery); "How much does an executive retreat cost?" ($5,000-$12,000/person Signature, $75,000-$500,000+ bespoke); "A retreat for a newly formed or post-merger leadership team"; "Signature vs. bespoke: which retreat is right for your team."
- [Ways to Work Together](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/ways-to-work-together): Two engagement tiers. Signature Retreats (Experiential Leadership Retreats / ELR) are ready-to-run, curated 4–5 star venues with exceptional food and a tailored content core, $5,000–$12,000 per person. Bespoke Retreats are designed from scratch around one outcome, $75,000–$500,000+ turnkey (the case studies are bespoke). Includes a white-glove path for executive assistants and chiefs of staff, and an interactive Physical/Emotional intensity tool. The Signature tier offers several interchangeable formats — four have their own pages (listed below); others, such as Open Water and Five-Star Estate, are described on this page.
- [Is This Your Team?](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/is-this-your-team): A symptom-matcher for leadership-team problems — big egos and turf wars, a new or merged team with no trust, a clash of work-ethic values, a polished team that can't get real, a scarcity mindset — each linked to the real anonymized case study that solved it. For executives searching for a retreat for a team that doesn't get along, won't collaborate, or needs to rebuild trust.
- Signature formats — each has its own page, is reinforced for 30 days, and tailors a content core to the client:
  - [Cabin Fever](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/formats/cabin-fever): remote-lodge retreat, close quarters — for trust and candor.
  - [Off-Road Immersion](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/formats/off-road-immersion): 4x4 terrain and shared adversity — for trust under pressure and interdependence.
  - [Winter Survival](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/formats/winter-survival): alpine cold and high stakes — to break stubborn divides and ego.
  - [Wilderness Expedition](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/formats/wilderness-expedition): river, alpine, and open water, deep off-grid — for alignment and shared command.
- [The Framework — The Lost Disciplines of Leadership](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/framework): James Carter's leadership framework and forthcoming book. One Flag (2-3 operational priorities everything serves), four disciplines (The Decision/Lost to Chaos, The Rhythm/Lost to Sprawl, The Standard/Lost to Avoidance, The Learning/Lost to Stagnation), one governing principle (Truth Over Comfort), one diagnostic (The 2Q: what are you creating? what are you allowing?), and a protective structure (Boundaries). It is a diagnostic lens, not a fixed program — retreats are always designed around the client's specific function.
- [Case Studies](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/case-studies): Real, anonymized engagements organized by the need each retreat solved.
- [Case Study: San Juan Mountains work-ethic divide](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/case-studies/san-juan-mountains-work-ethic): A biomedical engineering and manufacturing company's seven-person executive team was split into two camps over work ethic and work-life balance — one working 14–16 hour days, the other protecting boundaries — and they sabotaged each other rather than respecting the difference. Be Legendary ran a January winter-survival scenario near Silverton, Colorado (Eureka mining lodge, 9,300 ft): avalanche training, a staged stranding with quinzhee and snow-cave building under a "if you sweat, you die" rule, and a dog-sledding lesson about protecting "wheel dogs" (your strongest people) from running themselves to death. The two executives who overworked the shoveling were the same two who overworked at the office. Behaviors improved 268% over 30 days — Be Legendary's largest measured behavioral change. (Client anonymized.)
- [Case Study: Alaska executive vulnerability](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/case-studies/alaska-executive-vulnerability): A Fortune 100 executive team's fixation on appearing polished and professional built invisible walls that years of CEO coaching could not break, driving silos and near-zero cross-departmental cooperation throughout the company. Be Legendary staged a float-plane survival scenario beside a remote Alaskan lake; an embedded actor posing as a graduate-student filmmaker prompted each executive, one by one, to record a heartfelt message to their loved ones, dissolving the veneer into genuine vulnerability around a campfire. Be Legendary deliberately chose not to attach a behavioral metric so as not to cheapen the relationships; the result was the closest, most vulnerable executive team in 25 years of facilitation, with relationships still intact today. (Client anonymized.)
- [Case Study: Everglades abundance-mindset simulation](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/case-studies/everglades-abundance-mindset): A global professional-services firm's CIO and nine-person executive team were mandated to maximize existing resources rather than buy or build new, but competed and guarded turf instead of collaborating. Be Legendary ran a shelter-box survival simulation on a Miccosukee Tribe hammock in the Everglades, where strewn "trash" reframed instantly into valuable resources; the team's competitive scramble mirrored their behavior at work, and they never questioned two scarcity assumptions (that only the winning team earns a hotel bed, and that being split into teams means competing rather than acting as one team). Abundance mindset improved 113% over 30 days of daily behavior tracking. (Client anonymized.)
- [Case Study: Online auto retailer leadership team](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/case-studies/online-auto-retailer-leadership-team): A fast-growing national online used-car retailer had a virtual leadership team of star executives poached from rivals, whose egos became turf wars instead of building the business. Be Legendary designed a vehicle-themed retreat using staged airport encounters, an effort-and-priorities homework lesson, a public-transit empathy exercise tied to a single mother in a food desert, a constructed two-day desert survival scenario, and a culminating act of giving (filling and delivering a subsidized minivan to that family). Teaming behaviors improved 178% measured 30 days later via a behavioral habit tracker. (Client anonymized.)
- [Case Study: Federal fiscal leadership team](https://www.legendary-retreats.com/case-studies/federal-fiscal-leadership-team): A newly formed team of five executives from four formerly competing branches of a U.S. federal agency, working virtually across every time zone with near-zero trust, was forged into one executive leadership team responsible for a ~$1B budget via a series of retreats (one per time zone). The client then expanded the engagement to two further organizational layers. (Client anonymized.)
